name: Robert D. Foster
role: Nauvoo physician, later a publisher of the Nauvoo Expositor
dateNote: Section 124 named him on 19 January 1841; he was excommunicated on 18 April 1844.
importance: Robert D. Foster was an English-born doctor who joined by 1839 and travelled with Joseph Smith to Washington in 1839–40. Section 124 tells him to build a house for Joseph as contracted, repent of “his folly,” and buy Nauvoo House stock. In 1844 he broke with Joseph Smith and was excommunicated. He then became a publisher of the Nauvoo Expositor, whose destruction led to Joseph’s arrest.
connections: Section 124 tells him to heed Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, and William Law. He later joined Law’s breakaway church.

sources.title: Robert D. Foster, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Dates, excommunication and Expositor role checked on JSP and Wikipedia. The link from the press’s destruction to Joseph’s arrest is general knowledge.
